clue.text: Heavenly body, according to barker's pitch

parts.note: a barker is a dog, so barker's gives the possessive dog's
pitch is the black sticky substance also called tar

explanation.surface: A star's identity is decided by the sound of a dog's bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like the tone of the bark; it is the black stuff used on roads. The possessive apostrophe adds no letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is commonly called by this name, after the constellation Canis Major.

clue.text: May third turned out bright initially for the Bacchanalian celebration

indicators.note: turned out tells us May third is rearranged
initially picks out the opening letter of the word bright

explanation.surface: A bright start to the third of May for a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY THIRD rearranged ('turned out') gives DITHYRAM; add the first letter of 'bright'.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece this was a wild choral hymn sung in honour of Dionysus, god of wine.

clue.text: Battery-powered craft?

parts.note: suggests an electric boat, but a battery is also a group of heavy guns, so this vessel's power is its artillery

explanation.definitionFit: A small armed warship whose strength lies in its mounted guns.

clue.text: Traffic sign logo?

parts.note: traffic as a verb or noun means trade
a mark is a sign

explanation.surface: A road sign that serves as a company logo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic sign' looks like one road-sign phrase; it splits into commerce and a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered symbol identifying a company's goods, as a logo does.

clue.text: Gemstone of a type larger than pearl

explanation.definitionFit: A red precious stone; and in old printing, a size of type at five and a half points, just above the five-point size called pearl.

clue.text: Fit to drink, the river board found

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river, a crossword favourite
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A river authority has declared its water safe to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee; here it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Water described this way is safe for drinking, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Simple taps corrected this scratched old record

indicators.note: corrected tells us the letters of simple taps are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing some simple taps on an old scratched gramophone disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a vinyl disc; it is a manuscript whose earlier writing was scraped off to reuse the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript page scraped clean and written over, its earlier text often still faintly visible.

clue.text: Steps taken to make colour fade

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
to go is to fade, as of a fading light or failing strength

explanation.surface: Measures are taken to make a colour fade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' reads as measures taken; it is dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance from Argentina, and so a set of steps.

clue.text: Easily-broken track title, possibly?

parts.note: BR, British Rail, the former UK railway, whose lines are track

indicators.note: possibly says the word title could appear in another order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a track title on a record is fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the old national railway; 'possibly' turns TITLE into ITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragile snaps or shatters readily.

clue.text: Impatient, for example, to stand up during hearing

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another

parts.note: an ear is the organ, and sense, of hearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters for for example read upwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone impatient to stand up while a court hearing is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session; it is the sense the ear serves. In a down clue 'to stand up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and restless to get going is a near synonym of impatient.

clue.text: Secret society taking on a coach

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society

explanation.surface: A secret organisation recruits a sports trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' reads as a trainer, but it is a light two-wheeled horse carriage once used in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India this word names a light horse-drawn vehicle, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Evaluating a degree school

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
Lancing College is an English independent school in West Sussex

explanation.surface: Someone is assessing a school that awards degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING is a well-known English boarding school on the Sussex coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh up one thing against another is to assess or evaluate it.

clue.text: The old sign of those not quite gentlemen

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: An ancient symbol marks out men who fall just short of gentility.
explanation.walkthrough: Historically these landholders ranked just below the gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers owning their own land formed an English social class one step beneath the gentry.

clue.text: I am Bill the impersonator

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a bill is a printed notice, or poster

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be Bill, but is really a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a printed advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud who pretends to be someone else is a pretender or impersonator.

clue.text: Extra food on table is popular

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball out of the batsman's reach, scored as an extra run
a spread is a lavish meal laid out

explanation.surface: Laying on extra food at the table is a crowd-pleaser.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a WIDE is one of the extras, runs not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular in the sense of general or common among many people, such as a popular belief.

clue.text: Consultant radiologist shows cavities in bone

indicators.note: the consultant radiologist shows, inside the run of the two words, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A hospital X-ray specialist reveals hollows in a patient's skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy these are sinus-like hollow spaces in bones, the plural of a Latin term for cave.

clue.text: In the water off Cowes, a small number are on the rocks

annotationWithheld.why: In the water off Cowes, a small number are on the rocks: IN + SOL(V)ENT needs 'In' both as the letters IN and as the signal putting V inside SOLENT; no other word signals the insertion
annotationWithheld.clue: In the water off Cowes, a small number are on the rocks

clue.text: Album for the autumn?

parts.note: plays on an album with removable pages and the falling, detached leaves of autumn trees

explanation.definitionFit: A binder whose pages can be taken out, like leaves that come off trees in the fall.

clue.text: Ready-to wear quality for play?

parts.note: mixes the fit of off-the-peg clothes with the engineering sense of allowable variation, play in a mechanism

explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, the permitted range of variation in a part's size, so the margin or slack allowed.

clue.text: Minor burns

parts.note: read as small injuries from heat, but a burn is a Scottish word for a stream, so these are little streams

explanation.definitionFit: Small streams are rivulets; a burn is a Scottish stream, so minor ones are tiny watercourses.

clue.text: Difficult individual turning sour

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: turning makes the letters of sour go round into a new order

explanation.surface: A tricky person whose mood is turning sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges SOUR into ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdensome and hard to bear, as of a heavy duty.

clue.text: Bird of river and lake

parts.note: the Ouse is the name of several English rivers
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird that lives by rivers and lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in Yorkshire (and others share the name).
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the blackbird, also used for the ring and water varieties of thrush-like birds.

clue.text: Is one presented to the reluctant man-of-the-match?

definitions.text: Is one presented to the reluctant man-of-the-match?

parts.words: Is one presented to the reluctant man-of-the-match?
parts.note: sounds like a sporting award, but the match is a marriage, and an unwilling groom may be forced to wed at gunpoint

explanation.definitionFit: A forced wedding is named after the firearm an angry father points at the reluctant groom.

clue.text: Where sleeping infants may be troubled by wind in the air

definitions.text: Where sleeping infants may be troubled by wind in the air

parts.words: Where sleeping infants may be troubled by wind in the air
parts.note: suggests babies with colic, but recalls the nursery rhyme Rock-a-bye Baby, whose cradle sways high up when the wind blows

explanation.definitionFit: In the lullaby the baby's cradle rocks at the highest branches of a tree, and falls when the bough breaks.

clue.text: Egyptian king familiarly on gold coach

parts.note: Tutankhamun is familiarly known as King Tut
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A pharaoh rides in a golden carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' tempts as a carriage alongside the king, but it means a private teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher who instructs pupils is a trainer or coach.

clue.text: Poet describing Scottish Cup round?

parts.note: a tass is a Scots word for a small cup
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A poet writes about a match in football's Scottish Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish Cup' suggests the football competition; TASS is a Scottish word for a drinking cup. Torquato Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato, the sixteenth-century Italian poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Circuitous route of French excursion

parts.note: de is French for of
a tour is an excursion or trip

explanation.surface: A roundabout path on a holiday trip in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a longer way round taken to avoid an obstacle.

clue.text: Dicey way for players to get home?

definitions.text: Dicey way for players to get home?

parts.words: Dicey way for players to get home?
parts.note: sounds like a risky journey, but means a board game where dice move counters round to their home squares

explanation.definitionFit: A simple board game in which players throw dice to race their counters home.

clue.text: Hope chest, say, is tinted initially by le Douanier

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word tinted

parts.note: the customs officer, nickname of the French naive painter Henri Rousseau

explanation.surface: A bride's chest is painted in colour by a French artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Rousseau, the painter, was nicknamed 'le Douanier' because he worked as a toll and customs collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen, which in America is kept in a hope chest before marriage.

clue.text: Nigel Twist, marbles champion

indicators.note: twist tells us to wring the name Nigel into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Nigel Twist is the top player at the game of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7th Earl of this title brought the Parthenon sculptures to London; he champions the marbles in that he took up their cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl who removed the Parthenon sculptures to Britain, so his name is attached to them.

clue.text: One supports an arch reply

explanation.definitionFit: In architecture this is a half-pillar set into a wall to carry an arch; as a verb it means to answer.

clue.text: Jerseys may be found behind this lower rail

definitions.text: Jerseys may be found behind this

parts.note: something that lows, a cow or ox
a rail is a barrier, a fence

explanation.surface: Jersey cows graze behind a low rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerseys' looks like sweaters; they are the dairy cattle from Jersey. 'Lower' reads as less high but means a beast that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge with a guard rail built to keep cattle in, so a herd of cows stays behind it.
